analysis.subject: physics
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers weight definition versus aerodynamic forces, Newton gravitation law, formation of surface gravitational acceleration, weight equation linking mass and gravity, and example of weight reduction with altitude

overview.headline: Gravity as field force with mass distance law and altitude effect on weight

keyPoints.point: Weight differs fundamentally from aerodynamic forces like lift and drag that need air contact
keyPoints.quote: Weight is fundamentally different from the aerodynamic forces, lift and drag.

keyPoints.point: Gravity acts as field force that needs no physical contact with object
keyPoints.quote: The gravitational force is a field force; the source of the force does not have to be in physical contact with the object to generate a force.

keyPoints.point: Newton published his theory of gravitation with laws of motion in 1686
keyPoints.quote: Newton published his theory of gravitation with his laws of motion in 1686.

keyPoints.point: Surface gravitational acceleration value is 9.8 meters per square second or 32.2 feet per square second
keyPoints.quote: On the surface of the earth, its value is 9.8 meters per square second or 32.2 feet per square second.

keyPoints.point: Weight equals mass times gravitational acceleration as field force near earth
keyPoints.quote: The weight W, or gravitational force, is then just the mass of an object times the gravitational acceleration.

keyTerms.gloss: Force from earth attraction distinct from aerodynamic contact effect
keyTerms.quote: Weight is the force generated by the gravitational attraction of the earth on any object.

keyTerms.gloss: Field pull that acts without physical contact as described for earth
keyTerms.quote: The gravitational force is a field force; the source of the force does not have to be in physical contact with the object to generate a force.

keyTerms.gloss: Mechanical push from air requiring physical contact with object to generate force
keyTerms.quote: Aerodynamic forces are mechanical forces and the object has to be in physical contact with the air which generates the force.

keyTerms.gloss: Combined constant forming surface gravity from earth mass and radius
keyTerms.quote: the mass of the earth, and the square of the radius of the earth to form the gravitational acceleration, g.

keyTerms.gloss: Fixed value G used in particle attraction formula with distance squared
keyTerms.quote: a universal constant, G, times the product of the mass of the particles, m1 and m2, divided by the square of the distance, d, between the particles.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Distinguishes field versus mechanical forces to build correct mental model before introducing quantitative weight relations
componentPlan.focusQuote: Weight is fundamentally different from the aerodynamic forces, lift and drag.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Lets learners vary mass and surface gravity to see proportional weight change directly from stated equation
Reinforces key facts about surface gravity values and altitude weight loss with quick recall checks
componentPlan.focusQuote: If an airplane is flying at 35000 feet (about 7 miles) the distance to the center of the earth is about 4007 miles.
